messages:
maya: quick heads up — brought up quantized reranker-v2 (PTQ int4) in the eval harness and seeing ~3pt MRR drop on the longtail holdout compared to float32. baseline float32: MRR=0.421, NDCG@10=0.638; int4: MRR=0.391, NDCG@10=0.634. small sample but consistent across two seeds :frowning:
liam: ouch. did you use the exact same preprocessing/tokenizer and candidate ordering? often quant diffs surface from tiny input differences.
maya: yep same tokenizer files and vocab. eval command I ran:```
python tools/eval_harness.py --model reranker-v2-int4 --dataset longtail_holdout --seed 42 --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --batch 256 --truncate 1024
```
liam: can you paste the quant recipe? int4 can be sensitive to per-channel vs per-tensor scaling. also was kvpack enabled? that changes kv cache offsets which might affect determinism.
maya: recipe: `ptq_linear_perchannel` + default clip. kvpack disabled for this run.
sam: curious about sample size — how many queries in the holdout? also are candidates shuffled or preserved?
maya: holdout ~18k queries, candidates preserved (original order). did a quick seed sweep 42 & 99, both show similar drop.
eval-bot: summary uploaded — https://intra.redwood/evals/exp/1818887776 (contains run logs, diffs, and full metrics table).
nina: two quick checks: (1) truncation — float run used truncate=1536 historically, you ran 1024 here, could affect long docs. (2) embedding/candidate normalization — any L2 renorm differences?
maya: good catch. float baseline had truncate=1536; I accidentally used 1024 for the int4 run to speed up. rerunning with 1536 now. also no L2 renorm changes.
liam: please run a tiny ablation: int4 with truncate=1536, and float32 with truncate=1024 (to see truncation effect). keep seed fixed. also try per-tensor quant if you can — sometimes that reduces rank-order flips.
maya: starting the ablation; ETA ~40m for first pass. posting logs when done.
sam: if the drop persists after trunc parity, try reranking using doc-level candidate grouping (preserve anchor rank) — candidate ordering issues sometimes amplify metric swings for longtail.
maya: added to checklist.
liam: thanks. if results still bad after those ablations ping me and I'll run a cross-dataset check (core vs longtail) to see if this is distributional.
maya: will do. plan: (1) rerun int4 with truncate=1536, (2) float32 with truncate=1024, (3) per-tensor quant run, (4) candidate-ordering probe. I’ll post the numeric table here. :thumbsup:
 eval-bot: action: maya assigned `rerank-quant-ablation-1818887776` — due in 12h.
